text: Pneumonia. Important clinical notes: Pneumonia usually is caused by viral or bacterial infections. Pneumonia Description Pneumonia is an infective inflammation of the lungs. Patient Screening Cough, fever, and shortness of breath are symptoms that require a prompt, same-day appointment for medical evaluation. The use of analgesics, such as aspirin, helps to relieve chest pain, and oxygen therapy may be necessary for shortness of breath.
source: Essentials of Human Diseases and Conditions, 6th Ed.

text: Hypertension. Important clinical notes: Prognosis The prognosis varies and depends on the patient’s response to drug therapy. Choosing the best first medication is a continu - ous debate. text: Conjunctivitis. Important clinical notes: Conjunctivitis Description Inflammation of the conjunctiva, the mucous mem - brane that covers the anterior portion of the eyeball and also lines the eyelids, is called conjunctivitis. conjunctivitis is usually not a serious condition, although recurrences are common. Patient Screening The patient with corneal abrasion may experience significant persistent pain in the eye. Etiology Abrasions may be caused by foreign bodies being trapped between the cornea and the eyelid, by direct trauma to the cornea, such as being poked by a fin - gernail, or by the wearing of contact lenses that are scratched or poorly cleaned. T o identify bacterial or viral organisms, samples of the discharge can be taken for culture and sensitivity tests, although this is rarely necessary. 226 C H A P T E R 5 Diseases and Disorders of the Eye and Ear Symptoms and Signs The transparent outer covering of the eye is called the cornea. Symptoms of abrasion and ulcer include pain, redness, and tearing.

text: Diphtheria. Important clinical notes: Diphtheria Description Diphtheria is an acute communicable disease that causes necrosis of the mucous membrane in the respiratory tract. Diphtheria, unspecified) (A36.0-A36.9 = 12 codes of specificity) Refer to the physician’s diagnosis and then to the current editions of the Symptoms and Signs The patient, most often a child, has sore throat, dys - phagia, a cough, hoarseness, and chills. Patient Screening Children with fever, chills, and respiratory difficulties require prompt assessment. The patient is contagious for 2 to 4 weeks if untreated or for 1 to 2 days after initiating antibiotic treatment. Locally, the infection and inflammation cause grayish patches of thick mucous membrane to appear along the respiratory tract known as pseudomembrane, or false membrane. As the toxin is absorbed, it affects other vital organ systems, with many possible complications, including otitis media, pneumonia, myocarditis, and paralysis. Carriers, although infected, remain asymptomatic and do not contract active infection themselves. When a parent reports a child with respiratory difficulties, most protocols rec - ommend the child be seen in an emergency facility.
source: Essentials of Human Diseases and Conditions, 6th Ed.

text: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease. Important clinical notes: pelvic inflammatory disease, unspecified) (N73.8-N74 = 3 codes of specificity) Symptoms and Signs The infection is most common in young sexually active women, especially those with more than one partner. Pelvic Inflammatory Disease Description PID is an infection of a woman’s pelvis. Prevention The mechanisms that cause the disease are not clear, so no effective prevention is known. Sometimes the symptoms or signs are not clear; in that case laparoscopy can be helpful to confirm the diagnosis. Prognosis Without effective treatment, serious complications may develop. Other symptoms are those of an active infection: fever, chills, malaise, a foul-smelling vaginal discharge, backache, and a painful, tender abdomen. Danazol (a testosterone derivative) is rarely used because of the high frequency of unacceptable side effects. Although there is no cure, pregnancy, nursing a baby, or meno - pause may bring remission of symptoms because the aberrant tissue tends to shrink under these conditions. Prognosis Although no cure for endometriosis is known, a variety of treatment options are available. Symptoms and Signs Most fibroids are asymptomatic.
source: Essentials of Human Diseases and Conditions, 6th Ed.

text: Gonorrhea. Important clinical notes: Gonorrhea, also a common infection of the genito - urinary tract, causes symptoms and complications similar to those of chlamydia in male and female patients. Gonorrhea Description Gonorrhea, the second most commonly reported notifiable disease in the United States, is a sexually transmitted infection of the genitourinary tract. gonorrhea infection makes an individual more likely to acquire HIV , if exposed. Treatment Antibiotic therapy is given to both partners, begin - ning with a single injection, and/or followed with a course of oral antibiotics, such as azithromycin, eryth - romycin, or a 7-day regimen of doxycycline. Prompt treatment can cure the infection and prevent complications, such as PID and problematic pregnancy. Prognosis With early and complete treatment, the prognosis is excellent, even when there are complications. Patient Screening Males develop symptoms, if any, after an incubation period of 3 to 6 days. Etiology Chlamydia trachomatis, an intracellular bacterium, is the cause of chlamydia and usually is transmitted by sexual contact. Diagnosis T esting for chlamydia is most often done using a DNA-probe test, a test based on DNA detection.
source: Essentials of Human Diseases and Conditions, 6th Ed.

text: Gonorrhea. Important clinical notes: Prognosis Chlamydial infection can be cured with a complete course of antibiotics when taken as directed, even after symptoms subside. text: Syphilis. Important clinical notes: Syphilis begins with the presence of a painless but highly contagious local lesion called a chancre on the male or female genitalia (Figure 12-7). Syphilis is on the rise, especially in men, in the United States for the first time in many years. Diagnosis Standard screening tests are the V enereal Disease Research Laboratory (VDRL) test and the rapid plas - minogen reagent (RPR) test. Syphilis facilitates the spread of HIV . Syphilis can be transmitted in the first few years of the latent stage and in the first two stages. Syphilis cases are report - able to the local department of health.
source: Essentials of Human Diseases and Conditions, 6th Ed.

text: Chlamydia. Important clinical notes: Chlamydia Description Chlamydia, the most commonly reported notifiable STD in the United States, causes urethritis in men and urethritis and cervicitis in women. Chlamydia sometimes is called the silent STD because it often has no symptoms and thus it is sexually trans - mitted unknowingly. Chlamydia is a major cause of female sterility and a leading cause of pelvic inflam - matory disease (PID). chlamydia facilitates the transmission of HIV . A high percentage of women have no symptoms before dangerous complications start. Early female symptoms include dysuria, an odorless, yellow vaginal discharge with a burning sensa - tion, itching, abdominal pain, and dyspareunia. Patient Teaching Emphasize the importance of taking the complete course of antibiotic therapy as prescribed. Conversely, 75% of men have symptoms 1 to 3 weeks after exposure. Use of a protective barrier during sexual activity can help prevent transmission of chlamydial infection. Inform patients that meticu - lous personal hygiene and frequent hand washing are necessary to prevent spreading the infection to the eyes.
source: Essentials of Human Diseases and Conditions, 6th Ed.

text: Genital Herpes. Important clinical notes: Genital herpes is caused by herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2), and less frequently by HSV-1, and is a recurrent, incurable viral disease. Genital herpes can also be caused by HSV-1, especially in the younger population. Genital Herpes Description Genital herpes is an incurable, recurrent infection of the skin of the genital area, with ulcerations spread by direct skin-to-skin contact, causing painful genital sores similar to cold sores (Figure 12-5). herpes usually has prodromal symptoms, such as tingling, itching, or burning 1 to 5 days before the lesion(s) appear. Genital herpes is coded according to the site of the lesion(s). herpes con - tribute to emotional stress and social embarrassment. genital herpes must be watched more carefully for cervical cancer. Etiology T richomoniasis is a protozoal infection caused by T richomonas vaginalis and usually is transmitted through sexual contact. Treatment If the laboratory culture is positive, antiprotozoal drugs are given. After the antibiotic therapy, follow-up culture studies are ordered to ensure a complete cure because some strains are increasingly antibiotic resis - tant. Prevention Because this disease is transmitted primarily by sexual contact, prevention requires avoiding sex with someone whose sexual history one does not know. Diagnosis Laboratory cultures from the infected site (cervix, rectum, or throat) of infectious body secretions and microscopic examination of exudate with a Gram stain are performed to identify the N. gonorrhoeae organism. Ciprofloxa - cin, dual therapy of ceftriaxone and azithromycin, or doxycycline administration is started as soon as the diagnosis is made. See remarks under the “Prevention ” and “Progno - sis ” sections. text: Trichomoniasis. Important clinical notes: Although recent statistics indicate a decline in the disease rate, drug resistance to many antimicrobial medications is on the rise. Because transmission is also possible during birth, newborns must be protected from eye infections that can lead to blindness (Figure 12-4).
